question: How have Russian military losses in Ukraine evolved over the past 24 months — by category (personnel, equipment by class, territory) — and what does the trajectory of those losses suggest about the tempo and intensity of the conflict?

internal_scan.verdict: Zero internal candidates. Phase 0 returned 0 hits with score > 0; remaining results were filler. Proceeding to external.

indicators.name: Cumulative equipment losses by class
data_required: Per-loss-event record: date, equipment_type, equipment_class, side (Russia), confirmation_method
Loss-class taxonomy covering tanks, IFVs, APCs, artillery, MLRS, AD, aircraft, helicopters, UAVs, naval

candidates.rationale: Visual-confirmation OSINT register. Per-equipment row, photographic evidence, mature taxonomy. Gold standard for equipment.
Russian-side OSINT trackers; useful for cross-checking
Self-report; counts higher than OSINT. Useful for compositional shape but not absolute totals

indicators.acceptance: ≥18 months of daily-granular records; ≥10 distinct equipment classes; each row has a confirmation_method field

indicators.name: 30-day rolling equipment loss count by class
data_required: Same as F1.1 — derived in-flow via window function
indicators.acceptance: F1.1 acceptance met; rolling window computable

indicators.name: Week-over-week %change in equipment loss rate by class
Cumulative personnel losses
data_required: Per-day per-side personnel-loss count, with source attribution

candidates.rationale: Daily figure since invasion; widely reported but is a self-report and runs high
Open-source name-confirmed KIA — conservative ground floor
Cross-referenced KIA counter for Russian fatalities

indicators.name: Equipment-loss mix — % of total losses by class for last 90 days vs prior-war average
Top 3 equipment classes by recent loss share
Net Russian-controlled territory change
data_required: Daily sq-km estimate of Russian-controlled area in Ukraine

candidates.source: ISW interactive control-of-terrain map daily JSON exports
candidates.rationale: Daily polygons; the standard OSINT territorial reference

candidates.format: Web-rendered map; data behind interactive layer

indicators.name: OSINT confirmation lag — median days between loss event and confirmed listing
data_required: Per-loss row with both event_date and listing_date / confirmation_date

candidates.source: Oryx (oryxspioenkop.com) — listing date inferred from page-edit history; may require git of an Oryx mirror like Tom Cooper's CSV mirror

indicators.acceptance: ≥80% of recent-window rows have both dates

indicators.name: Share of recent-window losses with photographic / geolocated confirmation
data_required: confirmation_method field on each loss row

candidates.source: Oryx — confirmation_method is the implicit Oryx contract (every listing is photo-backed)

preference_order_rule: INTERNAL → DERIVED → EXTERNAL. Internal exhausted (zero hits); 6 of 13 indicators are derived from the same external source as their parent indicator.
approval_required_before_acquisition: External web fetch on first-time hosts: oryxspioenkop.com, mil.gov.ua, ualosses.org, isw.pub, deepstatemap.live
